correctness.rationale: Direct right conjugation in the semidirect product gives ((epsilon,a)*(delta,b))=(epsilon,(-1)^delta a+2 epsilon b). The proposed reflection relation is compatible with the formula and with inverse right translations; rotations are unchanged as individual classes. Subtracting the index expressions of the two medial sides gives zero for a rotational first operand and a sum of multiples of 4 in A for a reflection. Necessity is witnessed by (F_b,R_a,F_0,R_0), for which the two sides are F_{-b-2a} and F_{-b+2a}; varying a,b forces exactly the required pairs into every medial congruence. Minimality gives the universal property, and counting cosets on each cyclic factor gives the stated finite formula. These arguments apply to arbitrary abelian groups, including the trivial group and exponent-two groups where the two tags still differ.
residual_risks: The recorded twelve finite cases do not verify the infinite-family quantifier; the algebraic argument does. The uploaded script was not rerun.

evidence: In Dih(A), the derived subgroup is 2A: commuting a rotation with the involution produces its double up to sign, and quotienting by 2A makes inversion act trivially. Conjugation by a rotation of index in 2A fixes every rotation and adds an index in 4A to a reflection. Thus the derived-subgroup orbits are exactly the proposed classes, with the quotient table inherited from conjugation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is an immediate specialization, not a strengthening or an extra case that requires new machinery. Counting the inherited classes proves the remaining formulas and the trivial-congruence criterion.

evidence: The indexed result identifies the least medial congruence of the full conjugation quandle, using derived-subgroup conjugacy orbits. Bardakov–Sangare’s dihedral quandle R_n is not the full dihedral-group conjugation quandle; their full-group criterion concerns mediality itself.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The derived-orbit formulation is an equivalent universal quotient on the same objects when G is generalized dihedral. A quotient group by the lower central third term and a reflection-only dihedral quandle are not equivalent comparisons.

evidence: The indexed finite cyclic dihedral example gives the same four operation rules and m+gcd(m,4) cardinality. The primary paper gives the four-element S3 medialization.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The cyclic formula has exact coverage. The absence of a separate table indexed by arbitrary A is immaterial because the general orbit theorem also mechanically yields the invariant-factor formula.

originality.rationale: An earlier distinct indexed result proves the universal medialization of the full conjugation quandle for every group as the conjugation-orbit quotient by its derived subgroup. It also gives the cyclic dihedral instance with the same operation table and count. For an arbitrary abelian kernel, substituting Dih(A) into that exact general theorem yields all of the frozen statement by routine commutator and orbit computations. This is established coverage, not a priority inference from a title or a failure to access literature.
residual_risks: The indexed direct coverage is established without assigning original priority among the wider displacement-group literature or claiming that the indexed item is a peer-reviewed publication.
